recent_posts.title: Survey Sees AI Driving DevOps Productivity Gains Despite Challenges
recent_posts.summary: A Jellyfish survey of 636 software development professionals finds 64% report at least a 25% increase in developer velocity from AI, with 80% viewing AI as a net positive for productivity. Top AI use cases are code writing (53%), code review (49%), and code explanation (43%), with Claude Code, Gemini Code Assist, and GitHub Copilot leading adoption. Challenges persist: only 53% say AI improves code quality, 42% cite rising tool costs, and 36% face resistance from senior engineers. A growing gap is emerging between organizations that have mastered prompt and context engineering and those still experimenting. Only 43% rate their AI adoption as high or very high, and 64% say they still need better data to diagnose engineering productivity issues.

recent_posts.title: Bridging the IT Divide Without Breaking What Already Works
recent_posts.summary: Enterprise IT modernization of SQL Server infrastructure creates organizational tension between DBAs prioritizing stability and platform engineers pushing for automation and consistency. The key insight is that modernization doesn't require choosing between legacy and modern — it requires enabling both to coexist. High availability should be treated as a portable capability that follows workloads across on-prem, cloud, VMs, and containers. Organizations that succeed avoid forced timelines, resist introducing complexity for its own sake, and maintain uptime throughout the transition. The real challenge is alignment, not technology.

recent_posts.title: Atlassian Underpins Code Creation With New Agentic Insight Channels
recent_posts.summary: Atlassian's Team '26 conference showcased new agentic capabilities built on its Teamwork Graph, a knowledge layer with over 150 billion connections spanning Jira, Confluence, GitHub, and other tools. Key announcements include Code Intelligence in Rovo (early access), which lets developers and agents ask intent-level questions across multi-repository environments; AI Code Insights for contextual pull request reviews, proactive issue detection, and inline fix suggestions; and the Teamwork Graph CLI plus Rovo MCP Server, which give MCP-compliant agents standardized, governed access to organizational context. The platform positions Atlassian as a governance and context layer for AI-assisted software development workflows.

recent_posts.title: The Great Decoupling: Scaling the Outer Loop for the Agentic Era
recent_posts.summary: AI coding agents have dramatically accelerated the inner loop of software development, but the outer loop — PR reviews, security scans, compliance audits — remains stuck at human speed, creating a 'Velocity Paradox.' The proposed solution is an AI-SDLC built on Agentic DevSecOps: deploying independent, specialized agents inside the developer's IDE to handle security/secret detection, architectural guardrails, compliance verification, and database query integrity in real time. A key risk called the 'Inception Loop' — where the same AI that generates code also validates it — must be avoided through strict separation of concerns between generation and governance agents. The goal is a 'governance co-pilot' that matches AI development velocity without sacrificing enterprise-grade safety.

recent_posts.title: IREN to Acquire Mirantis to Reduce IT Infrastructure Management Friction
recent_posts.summary: IREN Ltd., a cloud infrastructure provider formerly focused on bitcoin mining, announced plans to acquire Mirantis for $625 million. Mirantis provides open source OpenStack and Kubernetes distributions and recently launched the k0rdent AI platform, which offers a unified control plane for managing bare metal, VMs, and Kubernetes environments. The acquisition aims to reduce friction for IT teams deploying AI workloads at scale, optimize GPU utilization, and lower total infrastructure costs. Mirantis will operate as an independent subsidiary while continuing to serve its 1,500+ existing customers.

recent_posts.title: Incredibuild Unveils Islo Sandbox to Isolate AI Coding Agents
recent_posts.summary: Incredibuild has launched Islo, a sandbox product that creates isolated execution environments for AI coding agents. Each agent gets its own dedicated environment, allowing DevOps teams to centrally manage agent identities, enforce guardrails, limit access to sensitive data and codebases, and control costs. Islo can be used standalone or integrated with Incredibuild's SDLC management platform. The company also announced a partnership with the Harbor Framework community to support reproducible agent benchmark environments. The launch addresses the growing challenge of safely deploying and governing AI coding agents at scale, as a Futurum Group survey found 60% of organizations are actively using AI to build and deploy software.

recent_posts.title: Reimagining AI-Assisted Coding for Team Scale in Enterprises
recent_posts.summary: Most AI coding tools are designed for individual developers, making them unreliable at enterprise scale where teams must adhere to standards, governance, and delivery processes. A more effective approach embeds constraints, structured specifications, and policies directly into the platform rather than relying on prompts. Key requirements include modular and versioned specs, intermediate design representations before code generation, system-level policy enforcement, machine-verifiable completion criteria, and built-in collaboration and auditability features. The distinction between a personal productivity tool and an organizational delivery system lies in how much the platform depends on individual skill versus embedded structure.

recent_posts.title: Cursor’s New SDK Turns AI Coding Agents Into Deployable Infrastructure
recent_posts.summary: Cursor has released a public beta TypeScript SDK that lets engineers invoke AI coding agents programmatically from CI/CD pipelines, backend services, or any part of the stack — not just from the IDE. The SDK exposes the full agent runtime including codebase indexing, semantic search, MCP server support, multi-agent orchestration, and execution hooks. Cloud execution provides sandboxed VMs with persistent, resumable sessions that can open pull requests autonomously. Self-hosted workers are supported for enterprise security requirements. Cursor's Composer 2 model is the recommended default, with token-based pricing for cost control. Analyst commentary frames this as Cursor positioning itself as infrastructure competing with CD platforms and cloud providers for the agent control plane.

recent_posts.title: The Trust Problem With AI Agents in Production Pipelines
recent_posts.summary: AI agents in production infrastructure can fail confidently without signaling uncertainty, creating dangerous automation complacency. Drawing on decades of research from aviation and industrial control systems, the author argues teams must design for calibrated trust: agents should expose uncertainty alongside decisions, dashboards should show rejected alternatives, and teams should practice 'trust decay' mitigation by scheduling synthetic escalation events to keep human operators sharp and ready to intervene when novel failures occur.

recent_posts.title: Anthropic Brings AI-Powered Security Scanning to Enterprise Teams With Claude Security
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic has launched Claude Security in public beta for Enterprise customers, an AI-powered tool that scans entire codebases for vulnerabilities and generates targeted patches. Powered by Claude Opus 4.7, it traces data flows and component interactions rather than relying on pattern matching, surfacing issues that traditional static analysis tools miss. Each finding includes confidence ratings, severity levels, reproduction steps, and recommended fixes. New features include scheduled scans, dismissal with documented reasoning, and CSV/Markdown export. Alongside the launch, Anthropic introduced Project Glasswing for securing critical infrastructure using the restricted Mythos model, and announced integrations with CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, SentinelOne, and major consulting firms.
